title: Token-path telemetry hub and failover scenario panels
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Build a unified token-path telemetry hub and a set of Grafana dashboard panels that make it trivial for SREs/PMs/engineers to: (1) pivot from a customer request to token-level latency and resource attribution, (2) see circuit-breaker/cutoff states and recent failover actions across regions, and (3) reason about adaptive load-shedding triggers that cause graceful degradation. This ticket covers the instrumentation additions, queries, dashboard JSON panels, and an incremental rollout plan.
background: Recent incidents highlighted two blind spots: token-level latency hotspots that do not appear in request-level SLOs, and slow operator feedback when a region fallback or capacity-tier downgrade occurs. Existing dashboards show p95/p99 at request granularity but do not connect admit/evict/caching signals into a single view. We want to create a token-path observability surface that correlates golden signals (latency, error rate, saturation, traffic) across each hop (router -> admit -> shard -> GPU -> model output) and surface circuit state transitions that preceded failover or shedding.
changes_required: 1) Instrumentation: add token_id tracing header and attach token-level timing spans to existing request traces; emit new Prometheus metrics: redwood_token_latency_seconds (histogram), redwood_token_kv_hit_ratio, redwood_token_admit_result_total{result="admit|evict|queue"}, redwood_circuit_state{region,shard}, redwood_failover_event_total. 2) Sampling: implement deterministic sampling (1/1000 full token traces, 1/100 of synthetic test tokens) and aggregate counters for SLI windows. 3) Dashboard: panels for cross-region token-latency waterfall, KV-cache heatmap by shard, admit/evict rate time-series, circuit-state timeline with annotated failover events, and a synthetic-scenario playground to replay admission failures. 4) Alerting: SLI-based alerts on token p99 degradation delta > 30% over baseline and circuit flapping detection. 5) Runbook and playbook updates with example queries and rollback steps.
implementation_notes: - Add a short-lived token_uuid on each request that is propagated through the router -> rpc -> serving runtime -> model. Avoid PII; token_uuid must be synthetic-only and not derived from request content. - Implement token_latency spans using existing OpenTelemetry spans and export summarized histograms to Prometheus via a gateway. - Use reservoir histogram (hdr/histogram) for p50/p95/p99 accuracy under high cardinality. - KV-cache hit ratio computed per-shard with labels {region,shard,model_variant}. - Circuit state exported as a discrete metric (0=closed,1=half-open,2=open) with last_transition timestamp label. - Storage: short retention (30d) for raw token-histogram metrics; longer (90d) for aggregates used in SLO retrospectives.
dashboards_and_queries:
Proposed metric names and example PromQL: 
- Token p99 (per-region): histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(redwood_token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le,region))
- KV hit ratio (per-shard): sum(rate(redwood_token_kv_hit_total[5m])) by (region,shard) / sum(rate(redwood_token_kv_request_total[5m])) by (region,shard)
- Admit vs Evict: sum(rate(redwood_token_admit_result_total{result="admit"}[1m])) by (region) / sum(rate(redwood_token_admit_result_total[1m])) by (region)
- Circuit timeline: changes(redwood_circuit_state[1h]) with event annotations from redwood_failover_event_total
Dashboards to ship: 
- "Token Path Waterfall" (stacked waterfall view of per-hop latency attribution)
- "Cache & Admit Health" (heatmap of KV hit ratio + admit rate per shard)
- "Circuit State & Failovers" (timeline + recent automated fallback events)
- "Synthetic Scenarios" (control panel to trigger synthetic token flows and visualize SLI impact)
acceptance_criteria: 1) Token-level histogram metrics emitted in canary region for at least 72 hours with sampling enabled and no >5% error on histogram buckets; 2) Grafana dashboard JSONs added to repo and rendering correctly in staging Grafana; 3) Playbook updated with run steps to interpret each panel and a documented rollback for a mistaken shedding policy; 4) At least two SREs and one PM review and sign off; 5) Alert rules validated in staging and bound to a paging policy with appropriate severity and suppression rules.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary-region): instrument and enable token sampling at 1/1000 for one region for 72 hours; validate dashboards and alerting. Phase 2 (controlled expansion): increase sampling to 1/200 and enable in two more regions, iterate on dashboard thresholds and refine histogram buckets. Phase 3 (global): enable full 1/50 sampling and final alert tuning; enable on-call escalation for circuit flapping alerts. Phase 4 (post-rollout): 30-day retrospective and metric drift review.
risks_and_mitigation: - High-cardinality metrics: mitigate by aggressive sampling and by aggregating histograms before long-term storage. - Latency within control plane due to tracing: ensure spans are lightweight and instrument only necessary code paths; run CPU profiling in canary. - False positives on circuit flapping alerts: tune noise floor and add minimum-event windows before paging. - Privacy: token_uuid must be non-identifiable and automatically rotated per-request.
